answer: A practical defense is requiring each participating agent to post a locked stake that can be slashed if the agent is later shown to belong to a Sybil cluster. The attacker must therefore allocate real capital to every fabricated identity; once the cluster is identified the entire set of stakes is confiscated. That linear capital commitment, together with the risk of total loss, makes large-scale faking expensive regardless of whether the attacker operates from a basalt ridge or paints the locked tokens saffron.
